Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:10:1.hebrew: מה נרצע אינו עובד את הבן - דכתיב (שמות כא) ״ועבדו לו״ ולא לבן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:10:1.english: Just as a pierced slave does not serve the son - For it is written (Exodus 21): "And he shall serve him," and not the son.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:10:2.hebrew: להעניק - בקרא דלעיל מיניה כתיב הענק, והדר כתיב רציעה, וכתיב בתריה ״ואף לאמתך תעשה כן״, ואהענק קאי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:10:2.english: To grant a severance gift - In the verse immediately preceding, it is written "you shall furnish [him] liberally" (haanek); and afterward the piercing is written; and after that it is written, "And also to your maidservant you shall do likewise," and it refers back to the granting of the severance gift.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:12:1.hebrew: אם כן - דלהקישא לחודיה אתא, נכתוב "ואף לאמתך כן", מאי "תעשה"? לאגמורי נמי אהענק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:12:1.english: If so - that it came for the comparison alone, let it write "And also to your maidservant likewise"; what is "you shall do"? To teach also regarding the severance gift.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:14:1.hebrew: דבר תורה - מדאיצטריך למעוטי עבד עברי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:14:1.english: By Torah law - Since it was necessary to exclude a Hebrew slave:

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:15:1.hebrew: משבאו לרשות גר אסור - להחליפם, דקמתהני מאיסורי הנאה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:15:1.english: Once they have come into the convert’s possession, [it is] prohibited - to exchange them, for he would be deriving benefit from items from which benefit is forbidden.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:16:1.hebrew: כי לא באו נמי - מכי מיית עובד כוכבים זכה בחצאין, והשתא קא מחליף להו. אלא ש"מ הא דיורש את אביו עובד כוכבים לאו מדאורייתא הוא, דאינו מתייחס אחר העובד כוכבים, וכקטן שנולד מאליו דמי, אלא מדרבנן הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:16:1.english: When they had not come [into his possession] as well - From the moment the gentile father dies, he acquired [his] halves, and now he is exchanging them. Rather, learn from this that the ruling that a convert inherits his gentile father is not by Torah law — for he is not considered a relative of the gentile, and he is like a minor who was born by himself — but rather it is by rabbinic law:

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:17:1.english: Lest he return to his [former] ways - Because of his money.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:18:1.hebrew: עובד כוכבים את הגר - כגון שנתגייר האב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:18:1.english: A gentile [inheriting] from a convert - Where the father converted.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:18:2.hebrew: וגר את הגר - אב ובנו שנתגיירו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:18:2.english: And a convert [inheriting] from a convert - A father and his son who converted:

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:18:3.hebrew: לא יחזיר לבניו - אם מת האב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:18:3.english: He shall not return [it] to his sons - If the father died:

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:18:4.hebrew: אין רוח חכמים נוחה הימנו - אין דעת חכמים נוחה עליהם במעשיו. כלומר, אין מחזיקין לו טובה, שלא הצריכוהו לכך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:18:4.english: The spirit of the Sages is not pleased with him - The mind of the Sages is not pleased with his actions. That is, they do not credit him with gratitude, for they did not require him to do this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:1:1.hebrew: למעוטי כו' - דלא תימא "אשר ברכך" רבויא הוא, וריבה הכל, וכיון דאיתרבי גדולי קרקע ובעלי חיים, (כל שכן) כספים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:1:1.english: To exclude, etc. - So that you should not say that "which He has blessed you with" is an inclusion, and it includes everything, and since the products of the ground (i.e., produce) and living creatures were included, (all the more so) money [is included]:

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:2:1.hebrew: הכל לפי הברכה - אם נתברך הבית בשבילו, הרבה תוסיף על הענקו; ואם לאו, אל תפחות מן הכתוב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:2:1.english: All according to the blessing - If the house was blessed on his account, give much more in addition to his severance gift; and if not, do not give less than what is stated in the verse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:2:2.hebrew: אם כן - דלהקישא לחודיה אתא, נכתוב ״ואף לאמתך כן״, מאי תעשה? לאגמורי נמי אהענק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:2:2.english: If so - If the verse came only for the analogy, let it write "and also to your maidservant you shall do likewise." Why [does it write] "you shall do"? To teach also about the severance gift.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:4:1.hebrew: עבד עברי עובד את הבן - אם מת אדוניו, עובד את בנו עד מלאת שש, או עד היובל הפוגעו בתוכם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:4:1.english: A Hebrew slave serves the son - If his master died, he serves his master's son until the completion of six [years], or until the Jubilee, whichever occurs within them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:4:2.hebrew: ואינו עובד את הבת - אם אין לו בן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:4:2.english: And he does not serve the daughter - If [the master] has no son:

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:5:1.hebrew: ולא ליורש - שאר יורשין, כגון הבת או האח:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:5:1.english: And not an heir - Other heirs, such as the daughter or the brother.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:5:2.english: He shall labor - Since it does not write "he shall serve you."

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:6:1.hebrew: שכן קם תחת אביו ליעדה - שמייעד אמה העבריה בכסף מקנתה, ואין צריכה קידושין אחרים, דכתיב (שמות כ״א:ט׳) ואם לבנו ייעדנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:6:1.english: For he stands in place of his father to designate her - For he designates the Hebrew maidservant with the money of her purchase, and she does not require other betrothal, as it is written (Exodus 21:9): "And if he designates her for his son."

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:6:2.hebrew: ולשדה אחוזה - המקדיש שדה אחוזתו, פודה בית כור זרע חומר שעורים בחמשים שקל כסף. ואם לא פדאה ומכרה גזבר לאחר, אין יכול עוד לפדותה, וכשיוצאה מיד הלוקח ביובל מתחלקת לכהנים. אבל אם לקחה בנו של מקדיש, אינה יוצאה הימנו ביובל להתחלק לכהנים. דהכי תניא בערכין (דף כה:): "ואם לא יגאל את השדה" — בעלים; "ואם מכר את השדה" — גזבר; "לאחר" — ולא לבן. או אינו אלא לאחר ולא לאח? כשהוא אומר "לאיש", הרי האח אמור. הא מה אני מקיים "לאחר"? לאחר ולא לבן. ומה ראית לרבות את הבן ולהוציא את האח? מרבה אני את הבן, שכן קם תחת אביו ליעדה ולעבד עברי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:6:2.english: And for an ancestral field - One who consecrates his ancestral field redeems it, at a cost of fifty silver shekels for a beit kor of barley seed. But if he did not redeem it, and the treasurer sold it to another, he can no longer redeem it; and when it leaves the buyer's hand in the Jubilee, it is divided among the priests. But if the son of the one who consecrated it bought it, it does not leave his possession in the Jubilee to be divided among the priests. For so it is taught in Arakhin (25b): "And if he will not redeem the field" — this refers to the owner; "or if he has sold the field" — this refers to the treasurer; "to another" — and not to a son. Or perhaps it means only "to another" and not to a brother? When it says "to a man," the brother is already mentioned. Then how do I explain "to another"? To another, and not to a son. And what did you see to include the son and exclude the brother? I include the son, since he stands in place of his father to designate her, and with regard to a Hebrew slave.

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:7:1.hebrew: אדרבה - מרבה אני את האח, שכן קם תחת אחיו ליבום! כלום יש יבום אלא במקום שאין בן? הא אם יש בן, אין יבום. והתירוץ הוא בניחותא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:7:1.english: On the contrary - I should include the brother, since he stands in his brother's place for levirate marriage! Is there levirate marriage except where there is no son? Thus, if there is a son, there is no levirate marriage. This answer is given in a settled manner [i.e., the Gemara's response is not a difficulty but a straightforward reply].

Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:8:1.hebrew: אלא טעמא - מאי דמצריך קרא מרבית לבן טפי מאח? משום דאיכא האי פירכא, דכלום יש יבום כו'. ומשני: שדה אחוזה נמי מהאי פירכא כו'. דאי לאו האי פירכא דכלום יש יבום, לא קיימא לן לרבויי בן טפי מאח. דהתם לא בן כתיב בהדיא ולא אח כתיב בהדיא, אלא משום דקם תחת אביו ליעדה, דכתיב בהדיא, הוא דמרבינן להו. ופרכינן עלה: אדרבה, מרבה אני את האח, שכן קם ליבום! ואיצטריך לשנויי עלה: כלום יש יבום כו', הא אם יש בן אין יבום. והתם ליכא למילף מדהכא תרתי והכא חדא, דהא חדא וחדא נינהו, אלא דאיכא יעידה בבן ויבום באח דכתיב בהדיא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 17b:8:1.english: Rather, the reason - What is the basis for including a son more than a brother? Because of this refutation, [namely,] "Is there levirate marriage [when there is a son]?" etc. And [the Gemara] answers: The ancestral field too [is derived] from this refutation, etc. For were it not for this refutation, "Is there levirate marriage...," we would not have held to include a son more than a brother. For there [regarding the Hebrew maidservant], neither "son" is written explicitly nor "brother" is written explicitly; rather, it is because he stands in his father's place to designate her, which is written explicitly, that we include them. And we refute it: On the contrary, I include the brother, since he stands in for levirate marriage! And it was necessary to answer this: Is there levirate marriage etc.? For if there is a son, there is no levirate marriage. And there, one cannot derive from the fact that here there are two and here one, for they are [really] one and one — except that there is designation for a son and levirate marriage for a brother, which is written explicitly.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 17b:16:1.hebrew: חליפי עבודת כוכבים קא שקיל - ואין לומר: טעמא משום ברירה, כלומר השתא הוברר הדבר דזה חלקו, דאם כן אפילו באו לרשותו נמי יהא מותר מהאי טעמא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 17b:16:1.english: "He takes an exchange for idol worship" - One cannot say that the reason is because of bereirah (retroactive clarification), meaning that now it has been clarified that this is his share. For if so, even if [the objects] had come into his possession, it should also be permitted for this reason:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 17b:17:1.hebrew: [אלא מדרבנן גזירה שמא יחזור לסורו כו' - והשתא לא הוי חליפי עבודת כוכבים, דחכמים לא תקנו לו ירושה כי אם בהיתר, דהם אמרו והם אמרו. וא"ת: אמאי יחזור לסורו? הא מיד שנתגייר כקטן שנולד דמי, ואם יחזור לסורו יש לו דין ישראל מומר! וי"ל: שיטעה להיות לו חלק ירושת אביו]. ת"י:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 17b:17:1.english: ["Rather, by rabbinic law; it is a decree, lest he return to his former ways," etc. - And now it is not a case of exchanging idols, since the Sages instituted inheritance for him only in a permitted manner, as they said [that he may inherit] and they said [that he may take the idols' value]. And if you ask: Why would he return to his former ways? Immediately upon converting he is like a newborn child, and if he were to return to his former ways, he would have the status of an apostate Jew! One can answer: Because he might mistakenly think that he has a share in his father's inheritance.] Tosafot Yeshanim.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 17b:1:1.hebrew: למר למעוטי כספים למר למעוטי פרדות - צריך לפרש: דמר ממעט כספים דוקא, ומר ממעט פרדות דוקא. אבל לפי ספרים דלא גרסינן וראב"י — כספים משבחי בעסקא, צריך לומר: למעוטי פרדות, וכ"ש כספים. ומיהו קשה: אמאי נקט כלל יקב? והא מכלל ופרט דלעיל מצינו למעוטי! לכך נראה לרבי דגרסינן: למר לאתויי כספים, ולמר לאתויי פרדות. והשתא איצטריך שפיר יקב, דאי לא כתיב יקב לא הוה מרבינן לא כספים ולא פרדות, דהוה ממעטינן תרוייהו מצאן וגורן. אבל השתא דכתיב צאן וגורן ויקב, הוי יקב כעין מיעוט אחר מיעוט, ואין מיעוט אחר מיעוט אלא לרבות. לר"ש אתא לרבות פרדות דוקא, דמשבחי בגופייהו; ולר"א בן יעקב לרבויי כספים דוקא, דמשבחי בעיסקא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 17b:1:1.english: "According to one Master, to exclude money; according to the other Master, to exclude mules" - We must explain: that one Master excludes specifically money, and the other Master excludes specifically mules. But according to the texts that do not read "and Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov" — [where the reasoning is that] money appreciates through business investment — one must say: [the term serves] to exclude mules, and certainly money. However, it is difficult: why did [the verse] mention the generalization "vat" (wine press)? Surely we find [a source] for exclusion from the generalization-and-specification [rule] above! Therefore it appears to the Rabbi that we read: "According to one Master, to include money, and according to the other Master, to include mules." And now "vat" is indeed needed, for if "vat" were not written, we would include neither money nor mules, as we would exclude both of them from "sheep" and "threshing floor." But now that it is written "sheep, and threshing floor, and vat," the "vat" is like an exclusion following an exclusion, and an exclusion following an exclusion serves only to include. According to Rabbi Shimon, it comes to include specifically mules, which appreciate through their own bodies; and according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, to include specifically money, which appreciates through business investment:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 17b:6:1.hebrew: מרבה אני את הבן שכן קם תחת אביו ליעדה ולשדה אחוזה - פי' בקונטרס: המקדיש שדה אחוזה פודה בית זרע חומר שעורים בנ' שקל כסף. ואם לא פדאה ומכרה הגזבר לאחר, כשיוצאה מיד הלוקח ביובל מתחלקת לכהנים. אבל אם לקחה בנו של המקדיש מיד הגזבר, אינה יוצאה מידו ביובל להתחלק לכהנים, דכתיב: "ואם מכר את השדה לאיש אחר ולא לבן". וא"ת, אמאי לא קאמר ליה נחלה, דבן קודם לאח? וי"ל דלא חשיב אלא הנהו דליתנהו באח כלל ואיתנהו בבן; אבל נחלה איתא נמי באח במקום שאין בן ובת:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 17b:6:1.english: "I include the son, since he stands in place of his father to designate her and for an ancestral field" - Rashi explained in the Kuntres: One who consecrates an ancestral field redeems it [at the rate of] a beit zera chomer of barley for fifty silver shekels. And if he did not redeem it and the treasurer sold it to another, when it leaves the buyer's hand in the Jubilee, it is divided among the priests. But if the consecrator's son bought it from the treasurer, it does not leave his hand in the Jubilee to be divided among the priests, as it is written: "And if he sold the field to another man, and not [to the son]..." And if you ask: Why did [the Gemara] not say to him [that it is because of] inheritance, since a son takes precedence over a brother? And one can say: [The Gemara] counts only those [cases] that do not apply to a brother at all but do apply to a son; but inheritance does apply to a brother as well, in a case where there is no son or daughter.
